info.description:
bmcproxy exposes one vendor-neutral HTTP API over heterogeneous BMCs (Redfish, AMI MegaRAC /api, IPMI) and picks the right southbound protocol per board and firmware.

## Request model (no stored secrets)
Every BMC request names its target and carries the BMC's own credentials:
- `X-BMC-Host: <ip|host[:port]>` (required) selects the BMC.
- `Authorization: Basic base64(user:pass)` is the BMC's own account, passed through for the life of the request (never logged, never stored; sessions are cached in memory only, keyed by host+user+hash(password)).
- `X-BMC-Vendor: <driver>` (optional) forces a driver instead of auto-detection.
- `X-Request-Id` (optional) is echoed back; one is generated otherwise.

## Tiers
- `read`: never changes BMC state.
- `write`: reversible (LED, boot override, power, time).
- `disruptive`: may cut connectivity or lose data (network, BMC reset, firmware, log clear). Returns 403 unless the proxy runs with `--allow-disruptive` **and** the request carries `X-BMC-Confirm: true`.

## Errors
Errors use the envelope `{"error":{"status","class","message","request_id","debug"?}}` (debug block only in debug mode).
| Status | Class | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | invalid_argument | malformed request |
| 401 | auth | BMC rejected (or request lacks) credentials |
| 403 | disruptive_denied / forbidden | tier gate or proxy policy |
| 404 | not_found | object or route not found |
| 501 | unsupported | capability not supported by this BMC/driver |
| 502 | upstream | BMC error, with vendor detail |
| 503 | busy | BMC busy, connection-capped or circuit open |
| 504 | timeout | BMC did not answer in time |
